correctness.rationale: The proof computes the nonsingular spectral derivative at P-eta Q, takes a justified linear-operator limit, optimizes the first diagonal functional over independently signed symmetric perturbations, applies equality-sharp Cauchy–Schwarz, and proves the unique mass optimizer. Differentiability yields actual finite-pair lower bounds, and Frobenius nonexpansivity gives the global upper bound. The asymptotic formula is derived from the optimizing critical-point equation. The embedded checker independently replays finite algebraic/numeric consistency tests; no finite experiment is treated as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact stratum invariant is naturally motivated by low-rank semidefinite repair. Its optimizer characterizes the worst eigenvector geometry, and its linear n/4 growth furnishes a substantive lower bound; coupled with Frobenius nonexpansivity it yields the new sharp order Theta(n) for global maximum-entry sensitivity. It addresses a robust functional-analytic boundary rather than a routine finite numerical slice. The precise constant for arbitrary matrix pairs remains open in this work.
